source_refs.claim_scope: UAVOS reports ApusNeo HAPS completed 100 hours 50 minutes from 2 November 2026 00:15 to 6 November 2026 05:05, maximum altitude 14,500 m, exposure to turbulence/high-altitude cloud/strong winds, flexible wing adapting through controlled bending and torsional deformation, and a protective coating on solar panels.

Canarias Stratoport / Fuerteventura Technology Park reports more than 3,000 km travelled, 14,534 m altitude, ApusNeo18 dimensions of 18 m wingspan and 12 m length, approximately 45 kg weight, and coordinated integration with commercial airspace during the November 2026 campaign.

owner_work_refs.responsibility: Whole-aircraft portfolio and matched mission MDO candidate taxonomy.
HAPS platform persistence and service comparison.
Wind-layer navigation and platform-specific aerodynamic/balloon control comparisons.
Demand-aware HAPS network service and edge workload placement.
Persistent-platform energy modelling and solar HAPS energy accounting.
Cell-to-installed-pack battery evidence and mission-conditioned aircraft storage qualification.
Mission electro-thermal coupling and temperature-dependent capability.

unknowns.reason: The public flight report does not provide a complete configuration manifest, build revision or instrumentation manifest.
The public source confirms a HAPS aircraft and solar-panel coating but does not establish the complete propulsion architecture, propulsor count, motor ratings or drive-train map.
No array area, cell type, conversion efficiency, incidence history, power trace or degradation data is supplied.
No installed pack chemistry, mass, usable energy, charge/discharge trace, reserve policy, state-of-health or full mission energy ledger is supplied.
The facility reports approximately 45 kg for the platform and nominal geometry; detailed as-flown mass breakdown, payload mass, CG and inertia are not supplied.
The source describes controlled wing bending/torsional deformation but does not supply a validated structural/aeroelastic model, strain/load measurements, fatigue life or gust-load envelope.
No time-aligned position, altitude, wind, attitude, irradiance, propulsion and weather trace is bound to this record.

The wider ISSEC project concerns wildfire/environmental monitoring, but this particular 100-hour report does not provide workload-level service quality, coverage, revisit, latency or delivered-data completeness.
No battery, motor, inverter, payload or avionics thermal telemetry and no qualified low-pressure thermal envelope is supplied.
Reported coordination with air navigation authorities is not a transferable operating authorization for another platform, operator or jurisdiction.
A single 100-hour flight does not establish multi-week endurance, 30-day availability, fleet reliability or maintenance turnaround.

assumptions: This is a source-bound reference candidate, not a Mira Aerospace as-built digital twin or a Luminous Dynamics design.
The candidate is classified as heavier-than-air HAPS; it is not a buoyant free balloon or buoyant airship.

The solar-assisted family label is used only to index the HAPS/solar-panel research lane; the actual propulsion architecture and the role of solar generation in propulsion/mission energy remain unknown.

The 100 hours 50 minutes flight duration and 14.5 km maximum altitude are source-attributed campaign values; altitude was varied during the mission and should not be interpreted as continuous operation at maximum altitude.
The approximate 45 kg weight and 18 m by 12 m geometry are source-attributed facility values; no mass breakdown or installed payload/energy mass is inferred.
The source-described adaptive wing is a research lead for aeroelastic/co-design benchmarking, not proof of a particular structural safety factor, fatigue life or superior gust performance.

This four-day campaign is not directly comparable to AALTO Zephyr's 67-day high-altitude flight or Sceye ST1's 30-day buoyant US-Japan round trip; platform class, altitude, mission and service boundaries differ.
No flight-performance, endurance, commercial availability, airworthiness, certification or operating-authority claim is made beyond the cited source-reported test campaign.
